review_question: Are security requirements written before the design, and does the design cover operation, maintenance and shutdown?
With no configuration changes, are all optional functions, ports, protocols and services off and all settings at their most restrictive usable value?
Does the design reuse vetted libraries and services instead of custom security code, and is each dependency maintained and patched?
Does the design assume that a compromise will happen, and are the cost to the attacker and the detection of an attack addressed?
For each identity, service account and process, what is the minimum permission set, for how long is it held, and who reviews it?
If one component is compromised, which data and systems can the attacker reach, and are those boundaries enforced technically?
Which critical actions need two independent parties or conditions, and can one person hold both roles?
Which mechanisms (databases, caches, credentials, temp storage, sessions) are shared between users or components at different privilege levels?
Is authorization checked on every request, on the server, for every object, and what happens after a permission is revoked?
If the primary control fails, which independent control still limits the damage, and does it depend on the same credential or component?
What state does each component enter on an error or timeout, and is that state denied or closed unless safety requires otherwise?
Which component, interface or process is the weakest, and has the highest risk there been addressed first?
Is there a simpler design that gives the same protection, and can a reviewer follow the security logic?
Would the system stay secure if an attacker had the full design and source, with only keys and credentials secret?
Does the control add so much friction that users will work around it?
Can operators configure, administer, upgrade and automate the control without error-prone steps?
